Ara / Milestone M2 / Windows / 27 October 2026

Outpost v0 is a playable co-op salvage run.

Solo, listen-host plus three clients, and dedicated plus four clients complete the real game in both the source project and the NativeAOT Windows export. Each network run includes late join, simulated latency/jitter/loss, private inventories, shared doors, a real drone downing and revive, extraction, and two verified authority replays.

M2 sign-off boundary: the game and recorded arabench baseline pass. Editor daily use is the lead's attestation. A separate multi-world C# host lifecycle defect remains routed to the engine owner; Outpost's menu is an art-only native world and its shipped gameplay uses one C# world per process.

Play it

D:\AraBuild\outpost-export\m2-outpost-20261027-ready\build\ara-player.exe

Open the executable for the main menu. Choose Play solo, or open it twice with --windowed, choose Host a crew in the first and Join 127.0.0.1:41090 in the second. Ready each scavenger. A dedicated host uses --game --dedicated --headless. Full source, export and editor steps are in samples/README.md.

Recover eight glowing caches, then keep every active scavenger at the blue beacon for three seconds before the five-minute nightfall. WASD moves; Shift sprints; Space jumps; right mouse drag orbits; E opens, loots or EMP-stuns; hold E to revive; Tab opens your satchel; Escape pauses. Three shared emergency rescues cover a missed revive.

1080p presentation review

All images below come from actual offscreen worlds and native UI. Original PNGs remain beside their gate reports. The menu vista has a slow live camera drift; the capture freezes one frame. Display lettering is limited to the title lockup, body text is readable, HUD panels are compact, teammate labels stay on one line and avoid the HUD panels, and controls fade after one minute.

Engine and authoring gaps fixed

  • Compatibility hashes: derive wire identity from sorted replicated schema shapes and policies. Process-role module sets, unrelated private fields and documentation no longer reject otherwise compatible peers; real wire changes still reject.
  • Replica presence: absent C# components no longer appear as empty objects or get projected onto every entity. The measured 20,000-read/650-row case fell from 80.005 ms to 1.509 ms.
  • Owner input: native sampling stamps queued actions on its actual input tick. One-tick E/Tab presses survive synchronization/input-delay shifts; mirrors refresh even while their clock is corrected or paused.
  • Tick-30 replay: restoring a tick-zero Jolt snapshot used to materialize absent motion/velocity mirrors and change authored pose bits before the first animation step. Restore now preserves exact optional mirrors. The focused regression went red→green; the original 6,111-boundary four-player extraction replayed twice, and every final gate verifies both a trusted and serialized portable replay.
  • Hash cadence: recording can sample tick multiples with Session::set_hash_interval(NonZeroU32), retains every input/command/stream boundary, and checks the final tick. Live bot recordings sample every 30 ticks; offline verification computes every tick and compares recorded checkpoints plus the live final hash.
  • Authoring and presentation: repeatable typed entity deletion; fully authored game/menu/animation/audio; enabled navmesh profile; runtime window-mode passthrough in the player; retained bundled body fonts; asynchronous frozen-data captures keep UDP polling while GPU readback runs. ara-samples build outpost now restores the game after rebuilding its art scene.

Hash cost and normal-session defaults

Full-scene sampleMean / median ms per hashEntities / ECS component instances
Final listen host, 12 samples, shared PC under focused-test load25.047 / 26.522667 / 5222; resources included: 685 / 5258; 65 reflected types
Final dedicated host, 12 samples18.747 / 17.833668 / 5238; resources included: 686 / 5274
Earlier quieter full Outpost scene19.573 / 17.875663 / 5,198; resources included: 681 / 5,234; 65 reflected types

Normal live sessions with no recording do not hash every tick. Keep hashing off for non-recording sessions; the API's default interval of one applies when recording hashes is enabled. A full hash can exceed the entire 16.67 ms simulation-tick budget, so per-tick full hashing is unsuitable for live Outpost recording. Dirty-column/incremental hashing could avoid repeated static-scene work, but it must cover provider state and serialization identity too; affordability is unproven until measured. No incremental implementation was added.

Remaining engine issue and verification limits

Multi-world C# host lifecycle: ara-script/tests/host.rs::two_worlds_drop_one_host_and_the_other_keeps_ticking reproduces the engine defect (9° observed, 18° expected after the first host is dropped). It is explicitly ignored in ordinary suites and routed to the lead/ABI owner, as requested for a change larger than focused ownership. The loader, slots, pending dispatch and HostInit callback context are global; both Init and Shutdown affect another live world. A Drop refcount alone is insufficient. Repro log: target/outpost-multi-world-repro.log. The menu remains the requested art-only scene.

cargo test -p ara-script --test host two_worlds_drop_one_host_and_the_other_keeps_ticking -- --ignored --nocapture

The editor's daily-use attestation belongs to the lead. Bot gates exercise real controls and networked simulation offscreen; they do not attest subjective audio mixing or physical desktop mouse feel. Join currently accepts numeric IPv4/port through the existing native text-input path. No store, relay or matchmaking service is required for same-PC play.

Reproduce with samples/outpost/tests/coop.ps1; add -ExportRoot D:\AraBuild\outpost-export\m2-outpost-20261027-ready\build for the packaged lane. Checkpoint logs: target/outpost-{build,clippy,fmt,focused-tests,hidden,export}-final.log. Assets restore through ara-samples fetch; generated media stays outside git.
